meta.status: EXPLORATORY, POST-HOC, DESCRIPTIVE. Development data already exposed to the research process; no new forecasting model fitted; segments chosen after the aggregate result was known; intervals condition on saved forecasts and do not include refit, selection or source-choice uncertainty.
meta.alcaraz: full_tier_entry (ARMS01 attempt 002 Arm 1), the frozen model named in the README
meta.sign: Every difference is left minus right in natural-log loss per match; negative favours the left (Alcaraz, or the later ladder rung).

bootstrap.cohorts: 21,561 ATP 2017-2025 (one weight matrix; priced-only statistics use the priced rows inside each draw); 2,681 ATP 2024 drawn separately with the same seed
bootstrap.sensitivity: calendar-week cluster bootstrap for BuildOak Part A (304 ISO weeks of tourney_anchor_date, same seed, 2000 draws)

segment_definitions.entry: panel a_entry/b_entry; Q qualifier, LL lucky loser, WC wild card; PR/SE/ALT and blank count as none. Wimbledon and US Open 2022 carry no entry codes in the source (245 targets) and fall in 'none'.
segment_definitions.level: panel tourney_level G, M, A, F. Best of 5 coincides exactly with Grand Slam in this cohort (4,361 matches each), so format is reported through level and not as a separate partition.
segment_definitions.round: panel round; RR (tour-finals round robin) grouped with QF or later
segment_definitions.lower_ranked_player_rank: max(a_rank, b_rank) from the panel (source ranking at the event); missing if either is blank
segment_definitions.rank_gap: |a_rank - b_rank|; missing if either is blank
segment_definitions.elo_favourite_tercile: terciles of |logit(pooled Elo probability)|, the ladder's Elo rung; cut points 0.3725, 0.8872
segment_definitions.rest: feature table rest_days_a/b (days since last eligible main-tour match, floor 2 at D-2, capped at 90; no prior match = 90). A long main-tour gap includes injury returns AND players arriving from lower tiers.
segment_definitions.workload: feature table matches_28d_a/b (main-tour matches in the 28 days to D-2); 9+ is about the top 5% of the max
segment_definitions.thin_history: min over the two players of prior primary-identity main-tour panel appearances dated on or before match_date - 2 days (panel starts 2005; Davis Cup and lower tiers not counted)
segment_definitions.completion: labels status retired or default (the result is still scored as in every published comparison)

buildoak.rival_has_alcaraz_lacks: Round, seeding, draw size, head-to-head, nationality and handedness match-ups, streaks, tournament-history and many rolling serve/return windows (443 columns, main-tour history from 1985), fitted with a recipe its author tuned on validation ROC AUC.
buildoak.alcaraz_has_rival_lacks: Qualifying, Challenger and Futures history (tier-inclusive Elo, experience counts, tier serve/return replay), opponent-adjusted dynamic serve/return states, and entry status (the pinned BuildOak ATP code drops every entry_ column), plus past-only proper-score calibration.
buildoak.common_input_control: The audit's shared-data control is WTA 2024 only (2,404 matches): on the same history and training keys Alcaraz leads by -0.0229 [-0.0325, -0.0140], and BuildOak loses 0.0219 when moved off its own data. No ATP common-input control exists in the docs read.

uts.rival_has_alcaraz_lacks: Head-to-head, set-level and indoor/outdoor Elo variants, winning percentages by round, level, opponent rank and handedness, and backhand traits, in a fixed hand-weighted formula over ATP history from 1968.
uts.alcaraz_has_rival_lacks: Lower-tier history, serve/return point statistics, workload and rest, entry status, and any weights or calibration learned from outcomes (the UTS weights are fixed).

ingram.rival_has_alcaraz_lacks: A generative point-level structure: serve and return point-win abilities by surface, turned into match probabilities through the scoring system (best-of-3 vs 5).
ingram.alcaraz_has_rival_lacks: Rankings, workload and rest, lower-tier history, entry status, player traits, a learned non-linear combiner and past-only calibration (the adaptation fixed 'no extra calibrator').

g_l_baselines.rival_has_alcaraz_lacks: Nothing Alcaraz lacks in kind: each is one rating (pooled, Kovalchik, FiveThirtyEight surface or weighted Elo) or the ranking alone, from main-tour history; WElo also weights by game share.
g_l_baselines.alcaraz_has_rival_lacks: Everything beyond a single rating: serve/return, rankings plus Elo together, workload, lower-tier history, entry status and a learned combiner.
